market_name: Will 1 Fed rate cut happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market's implied probability move is confirmed and sizeable (>5 points) rather than thin-liquidity noise; compare with fed funds futures/OIS repricing.
time_plan.1h: Watch 2y and 10y Treasury yields and TLT intraday tape for corroboration of a dovish/hawkish shift.
time_plan.2h: Cross-check against any Fedspeak, CPI/PCE, or jobs-data catalysts that could independently explain both the market and asset move (avoid false attribution).
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether the move persists or mean-reverts; note that a single-day full-year cut probability rarely drives durable long-end moves.
time_plan.12h: Record realized TLT return vs. expectation; flag if the anomaly preceded a public catalyst (leak test) or simply tracked already-public rate expectations.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of at least one 2026 Fed cut signals a more dovish expected path. Lower expected policy rates pull down the long end of the curve, lifting long-duration Treasury prices (TLT). The linkage is directionally clean but the baseline probability of at least one cut over a full year is already very high and largely priced, so incremental information content is limited. If instead the probability fell (hawkish repricing), TLT would fall.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm the probability shift is genuine and check DXY/EUR-USD reaction.
time_plan.1h: Compare US OIS repricing against foreign rate expectations to gauge differential move.
time_plan.2h: Screen for confounding macro releases or risk-off flows that move the dollar independently.
time_plan.6h: Assess persistence vs. reversal; the FX channel often decouples from a single rate-path market.
time_plan.12h: Log realized UUP return and whether the FX move was attributable to the rate-path repricing or unrelated drivers.

predictions.reasoning: A higher implied probability of Fed cuts narrows expected US rate differentials, which tends to weaken the dollar (UUP down). This is a second-order, weaker channel than the Treasury link and is easily overwhelmed by relative moves in ECB/BoJ expectations, risk sentiment, and global flows, so exposure is diffuse and confidence low.

evidence_used: Market question tracks the number of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a direct read on expected monetary policy path
Standard transmission: lower expected policy rates -> lower yields, higher bond prices, weaker dollar, supportive for rate-sensitive equities and gold
Baseline probability of at least one cut over a full calendar year is structurally high and largely embedded in fed funds futures/OIS
uncertainty_notes: Direction of any asset move depends entirely on which way the implied probability moved; the card is written pre-move, so both up and down scenarios are possible
At least one cut over 12 months is a low-information, likely already-priced outcome; marginal signal is weak
12h horizon is too short for a full-year policy-path market to produce large asset moves; nothing here approaches the 700bp tradable threshold
Topic tag 'military_conflict' appears mislabeled; this is a monetary-policy market

llm_justification.summary: This is a US monetary-policy probability market. A sharp rise in the implied odds of at least one 2026 Fed cut maps to a modestly dovish repricing: long Treasuries (TLT) up and the dollar (UUP) down, with the reverse on a hawkish shift. Both channels are directionally standard but weak in a 12h window because a full-year 'at least one cut' outcome is already largely priced, giving low information content. No implication reaches the 700bp tradable bar; confidence is deliberately low.
key_assumptions: The market proxies expected Fed policy path via cut count for 2026
Standard rate-transmission channels hold over the window
A probability increase reflects a genuine dovish repricing rather than liquidity noise or resolution mechanics
failure_modes: The outcome (at least one cut in a year) is near-certain and already public/priced, so any market move carries little new info
Direction assumption inverts if the implied probability actually fell (hawkish)
Proxy exposure is diffuse: TLT and UUP respond to global rates, risk sentiment, and scheduled data that can dominate any single-market signal
12h window is far too short for a full-year policy market to move assets 700bp; likely non-tradable noise
Possible confounding by a concurrent public macro release causing false attribution
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
